name: redis3m
listed_description: Wrapper of hiredis with clean C++ interface, supporting sentinel and ready to use patterns.
reason: C++ client wrapper over hiredis. README (opened) has goals, install and docs only; repo has no benchmark directory (top level: examples, include, src, tests, data/lua). No numeric or directional speed claim against hiredis, redox or any other client.

name: SimDB
listed_description: High performance, shared memory, lock free, cross platform, single file, minimal dependencies, C++11 key-value store.
reason: Only number is an informal absolute rate in README: 'conservatively' 500,000 small get() and put() calls per logical core per second, with the author stating 'Real benchmarking needs to be done'. No named baseline (no std::map, RocksDB or other store), no benchmark code (repo has only simdb.hpp, ConcurrentMap.cpp, README); one WebSearch found no third-party comparison.

name: SOCI
listed_description: A database abstraction layer for C++.
reason: Abstraction layer over native client libraries; README (opened) and docs file list contain no performance claim. The only numbers found are a 2008 CppCMS blog (snippet only, not opened) measuring SOCI roughly 38 to 48 percent slower than native MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite3 drivers, so no faster-than-baseline claim exists.

name: sparkey
listed_description: Simple constant key/value storage library. Designed for read-heavy loads with infrequent, large bulk inserts.
reason: README (opened) benchmark (src/bench.c, Xeon L5630 2.13GHz) reports only Sparkey's own numbers (for example 1,724,692 lookups/cpusec at 1000 elements, 503,818 at 100M) and no other store; bench.c has only Sparkey candidates (uncompressed, snappy, zstd). Comparisons to CDB and Tokyo Cabinet are qualitative ('comparable'). A Hacker News comment (snippet only) reports LMDB creating faster than Sparkey, so no faster-than-baseline claim.
